questions.title: What does the bound guarantee?
paragraphs: A stable closed-loop transfer T maps disturbance w to output z, with zero initial state.
Its H∞ norm is at most 2.
State the resulting L2-norm bound. Does it also imply |z(t)| ≤ 2|w(t)| at every instant?

questions.title: A small-gain certificate
paragraphs: A well-posed feedback loop connects stable blocks M and Δ.
You know ||M||∞ = 2 and ||Δ||∞ ≤ δ.
What range of δ gives a strict small-gain stability certificate? What can this test conclude at δ = 0.5?

questions.title: Which Riccati root?
paragraphs: For dx/dt = x + u, minimize J = ∫₀∞ (x² + u²) dt.
The scalar Riccati equation is 2P − P² + 1 = 0, with u = −Px.
Which root gives the stabilizing LQR solution? Give its closed-loop pole.

questions.title: Scaling both cost weights
paragraphs: A standard unconstrained infinite-horizon LQR problem has a unique stabilizing gain K.
Replace Q by 10Q and R by 10R, leaving the dynamics unchanged.
Does K change? What happens to the optimal cost? Explain without solving a Riccati equation.

questions.title: Poles after adding an estimator
paragraphs: A continuous-time LQG controller uses u = −Kx̂ and a Kalman estimator.
A − BK has poles −1 and −2. A − LC has poles −3 and −4.
What are the four poles of the nominal combined system? Explain the separation argument.

questions.title: A noisier sensor
paragraphs: In a standard unconstrained LQG design, keep A, B, C, the process noise and the LQR cost weights fixed.
Increase only the measurement-noise covariance.
Must the LQR state-feedback gain K change? Which design must be recomputed, and why?

questions.title: Accelerate, then brake
paragraphs: A unit-mass particle obeys dx/dt = v, dv/dt = u, |u| ≤ 1.
Move from (x,v) = (0,0) to (1,0) in minimum time.
Give the two bang values, the switching time and the total time. Briefly justify the times.

questions.title: When the switching function vanishes
paragraphs: Use the MINIMIZATION convention for a Hamiltonian H = H₀ + φ(t)u, with |u| ≤ 1.
Give the minimizing u when φ > 0 and when φ < 0.
If φ is zero throughout an interval, does this condition determine u there? Name this type of arc.

questions.title: Beyond a non-increasing V
paragraphs: Consider dx/dt = y and dy/dt = −x − y³.
Take V = (x² + y²)/2.
Compute dV/dt. Can you conclude global asymptotic stability of the origin? Identify the invariant-set argument.

questions.title: A local result has limits
paragraphs: For dx/dt = −x + x³, the linearization at the origin is dx/dt = −x.
Is the origin globally asymptotically stable? Find its exact region of attraction on the real line and explain what limits it.

questions.title: Exact feedback linearization
paragraphs: A system has full-state measurements and no input limits:
dx₁/dt = x₂
dx₂/dt = sin(x₁) + (1 + x₁²)u.
Choose u(x₁,x₂) so that d²x₁/dt² + 3 dx₁/dt + 2x₁ = 0.
Is your feedback singular anywhere?

questions.title: Attraction to a cycle
paragraphs: In polar coordinates, a planar system obeys dr/dt = r(1 − r²), dθ/dt = 1.
For any initial radius r > 0, what motion attracts the trajectory?
If two trajectories start on that motion with different phases, do their positions converge to each other?
